Field Verification Standard: Apply Citizenship in the Nation Requirement 1 procedures using verifiable measurements, clear terminology, and the BSA EDGE method.

Counselor Conference Readiness: Record concrete observations, examples, and sketches in your Citizenship in the Nation Workbook before requesting Requirement 1 sign-off.
step_by_step_procedure: Prepare & Inspect (Req 1): Review the official Citizenship in the Nation requirement standard and verify all required tools, reference tables, and safety gear.
Analyze Core Principles: Identify the primary concepts, definitions, and cause-and-effect relationships governing What is the Constitution of the United States?.
Execute & Document: Perform the what task methodically with your patrol buddy and log specific observations in your Citizenship in the Nation Workbook.
Verify With Counselor: Present your completed work, demonstrate proficiency, and answer Socratic check-for-understanding questions for Blue Card sign-off.

Tell your counselor what you learned about the landmark or site and what you found interesting about it. (b) Tour your state capitol building or the U.S. Capitol. Tell your counselor what you learned about the capitol, its function, and the history. (c) Tour a federal facility. Explain to your counselor what you saw and what you learned about its function in the local community and how it serves this nation. (d) Choose a United States national monument that interests you. Using books, brochures, the internet (with your parent or guardian's permission), and other resources, find out more about the monument. Tell your counselor what you learned, and explain why the monument is important to this country's citizens.
